gap: No result ChatGPT got states that ViewSonic's own US page for the VG1457 (the $349.99 14-inch dual screen ChatGPT listed as a two-added-screen trading pick) says dual-screen Extend mode is unavailable on macOS because of MST limits, and only the lower display turns on. On a MacBook it adds one extended screen, not two.
standout_why: I checked the cited Macworld 'Best portable monitors for Mac' page, the cited Xebec comparison page and the itechguides '15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026' page. Macworld mentions neither the VG1457 nor MST. It covers the base-chip limit only for the Trio 3 Pro: plain M1/M2 Macs and the MacBook Neo can connect one monitor and need free software. The itechguides page does not cover the VG1457 or the ZenScreen Duo and never mentions MST. The Xebec page covers only Xebec units. ChatGPT's answers asked 'What laptop do you use? MacBook' but never said that one of its four picks cannot extend to both screens on macOS.
decides: For a trader on a MacBook, the ViewSonic VG1457 drops out as a two-screen pick: its maker says only one screen extends. ASUS says the ZenScreen Duo needs its USB-C2 port for Extend, and that a Mac USB-C port 'with an AMD graphics card' extends to only one external display. That note covers Intel-era AMD MacBook Pros, not Apple-silicon Macs, so it needs care. The Xebec Tri-Screen 3 costs $699 plus a $59 adapter that Xebec says every MacBook Air and Pro needs, $758 in all on a Mac on 2026-11-21. Prices for the Aura dual screens, the UPERFECT Delta and the ASUS Duo could not be read today (rate limits and timeouts), so the price ranking among the cheaper two-screen units is incomplete. The Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro (ours, 2 × 2240×1400) still has the sharpest panels of the sourced two-screen units for dense chart layouts. On base M1/M2 Macs it needs Mobile Pixels' driver, per Macworld. That confirms ChatGPT's top pick for Pro/Max MacBooks and Windows laptops with two video-capable USB-C ports.
